_about: Golden retrieval set for calibrating vector search (P2-2).
Each 'positive' is a question the ingested corpus genuinely answers, with
the source_name(s) whose chunks are the correct evidence. Every expected
source below was read out of the live embedding_chunk table, not invented:
if you re-ingest a different corpus this file must be rewritten, and
scripts/calibrate_retrieval.py will tell you so by reporting sources it
Each 'negative' is a question about a plausible customer topic the corpus
does NOT cover. Negatives are what make the absolute similarity floor
measurable: without them you can tune recall to 100% by setting the
threshold to zero and never learn what that lets through.
The set is sized to the corpus (27 live chunks across 9 sources), not to a
round number. It is large enough to place the floor and to catch a
regression; it is NOT large enough to justify fine-grained claims about
small differences in recall. Grow it as the corpus grows.
